_: The tongue: a muscular hydrostat (intrinsic longitudinal, transverse and vertical fibres plus extrinsic genioglossus etc.) covered on the dorsum by a papillated mucosa (filiform, fungiform, circumvallate, foliate) and a saliva film. Stiffness values are for the relaxed tongue at rest, awake; active contraction stiffens it. Adult. Materials research lane, mouth group, 2026-11-07.

alpha.src: the dorsum's filiform papillae (195 um high, 160 per cm2, ANDABLO20) make a velvety, diffuse surface; GGX cannot hold that relief, so a high alpha stands in at the pixel scale while the papillae are geometry/displacement
liquid film draped over papillae (not flat)

circumvallate.src: encyclopaedia citing Gray 2008 (via MTT section 6, weak)

colour_Lab.src: not found: no instrument tongue-dorsum colour retrieved (MTT section 11)

translucency.v: the filiform papillae's keratinised tips scatter (whitish tint, thicker coating = whiter); fungiform papillae look as red dots (thin epithelium over vessels)

kinetic.src: RANC06 piglet tongue: saliva layer lowers dynamic friction x1.6; porcine tongue minimum ~0.35 with artificial saliva (thesis via search); BONGAERTS07 PDMS + saliva ~0.02; ANDABLO20 tongue-replica surfaces 0.1-0.5 with xanthan / whey lubricants (no saliva). No in vivo human value

friction.counterface: tongue replicas, pig tongue; see pairs/mouth.json

tack.v: saliva mucins give a lubricating, slightly mucoadhesive layer; tongue-palate seal during swallowing is by pressure, not adhesion

water_contact_angle_deg.src: ANDABLO20 pig tongue ~77 deg (proxy); RANC06 hydrophobic-leaning without saliva, hydrophilic with it

collision_thickness_mm.src: ASSY23 anterior tongue saliva film 68.9 um

contact_stiffness_kPa_per_mm.src: whole-tongue E 8.94 kPa (3 x BROWN15 G) over its 39.4 mm thickness (MTT R21); local indentation is better done Hertzian

contact_damping_ratio.src: hydrated soft tissue contacts are heavily damped; muscle 0.14-0.42 (MUSCLE damping_ratio); 0.3 a middle value

response_time_ms.src: a slow, soft body: shear waves cross 40 mm at ~1.7 m/s in ~24 ms

damping_ratio.src: hydrated soft tissue contacts are heavily damped; muscle 0.14-0.42 (MUSCLE damping_ratio); 0.3 a middle value

thickness_mm.src: not measured; filiform papillae alone 0.2 mm high (ANDABLO20)

compressible_to_fraction.src: papillae bend and flatten under load (ANDABLO20 surfaces)

thickness_mm.src: MTT R21 thickness 39.4 mm minus mucosa

compressible_to_fraction.src: near-incompressible (muscular hydrostat: shape changes, volume does not): a layer thins only by flowing sideways; 0.95 of thickness under ordinary contact, more under sustained load

thickness_mm.src: the base of the tongue: muscle insertions, not a flat bone

deform.model_note: muscle body with fibre directions per region (DTI); viscoelastic; incompressible (a muscular hydrostat keeps its volume while changing shape)

shear_kPa.src: BROWN15 controls 2.98 +- 0.44 kPa (80 Hz MRE); CHENG11 2.67 +- 0.29 kPa (7 volunteers); SWE_TW 21.5 +- 8.1 kPa (ultrasound, whole tongue, regional 18-25). MRE and SWE differ ~7x by method and frequency

E_kPa.src: E = 3G from BROWN15 MRE storage modulus (incompressible); SWE implies ~20 kPa or more

anisotropy.src: BROWN15 OSA tongues 0.94 +- 0.19 (no CPAP) and 1.08 +- 0.10 (CPAP); control ratio in Table 3 not retrieved. At rest the tongue is near-isotropic in shear; along-fibre stiffness rises with activation (MUSCLE: passive skeletal muscle ~20:1 in tension)

loss_modulus.src: not retrieved: BROWN15 Table 3; loss modulus correlates with BMI (R 0.53)

active.v: contraction stiffens the muscle (cf. MUSCLE shear 4.0 relaxed -> 9.5 kPa at 20 % MVC)

dry.src: dry mouth: friction rises (RANC06 x1.6 without saliva; BONGAERTS07 dried saliva mu 2-3 on model surfaces)

coated.src: a whitish coat of desquamated cells and debris between the filiform papillae (clinical description); no numbers

contracted.src: x3 by analogy with skeletal muscle at moderate activation (MUSCLE 4.0 -> 9.5 kPa at 20 % MVC)
